premise.statement: Every reachable nonterminal root-phase call site not already decided by an exact terminal lane admits either an ordinary exact N^2-capped pivot or a frozen exact v2 B2 macro followed atomically by a roots_only exact N^2-capped elimination with strict progress.

lemma.statement: If L1 holds universally for the frozen algorithm, then every reachable root-phase state remains within the fixed input-relative N^2 state envelope, every state-changing root-phase transition is exact and strict-progress, the number of state-changing root-phase transitions is O(N), and exhaustive deterministic discovery/verification work and retained proof resources in the root phase are bounded by a fixed polynomial in the original normalized input size N.
proof: Initial normalized root state has state_units<=N<=N^2.
Unit propagation and exact terminal lanes do not require promotion outside the admitted exact semantics; unit propagation only removes satisfied clauses/literals before canonicalization.

An admitted ordinary elimination is accepted only when eliminate_var_capped returns before the frozen raw N^2 cap and exact replay verifies the transition; the retained canonical state can only be smaller than the charged raw representation.

An admitted v2 transition checks the exact definitional macro representation against the same N^2 state cap, exact-replays the macro, then exact-eliminates a live original root under N^2 and accepts only strict progress.
Under L1, whenever the exact terminal portfolio declines to decide and roots remain, one of those two admitted move types exists. Therefore induction preserves state_units<=N^2 throughout root phase.

The previously proved retained-live-variable invariant gives at most N live variables and at most N successful v2 births over root phase. Each ordinary successful elimination removes a live variable; each successful v2 atomically removes one live root. Hence the number of root-phase state-changing moves is O(N).
The ordinary grammar has at most N pivots. The v2 grammar has at most four sign choices for each unordered pair of at most N underlying live variables, hence at most 4*binom(N,2)=O(N^2) pair types.

At any state_units<=N^2, clause count and literal occurrence count are each <=N^2 and every clause width is <=N. Exact ordinary elimination examines at most O(N^4) parent pairs; per-pair literal/set work is polynomial, and canonical duplicate/subsumption processing over an explicit <=polynomial-size candidate representation is polynomial.

For each v2 pair candidate, macro construction/replay scans an explicit <=N^2 state and then invokes at most N exact root-pivot probes, each with the preceding polynomial elimination/verification bound. Multiplying by O(N^2) v2 candidates remains a fixed polynomial in original N.

All generated root-phase extension identifiers are O(N) by the proved <=2N global birth bound, hence identifier bit length is O(log N). Event/certificate payloads contain only polynomially many explicit literals, identifiers, hashes, counters and exact transition data per polynomially many probes; no exponentially large hidden integer or identifier is introduced by the frozen grammar.
Therefore L1 discharges the root-phase part of input-relative reachable preservation, polynomial discovery/work, polynomial state-changing step count and explicit-resource accounting.

coarse_work_note.claim: No optimized exponent is needed for the composition bridge. The proof requires only existence of one fixed polynomial exponent for the frozen explicit algorithms.
coarse_work_note.warning: An implementation-specific tighter exponent should not replace the coarse symbolic polynomial bound unless separately audited in bit complexity.
